why: The Washington County moratorium (ORD-2026-12) is in effect as of 2026-10-26 and applies countywide, deferring acceptance and approval of all data center applications until 2027-06-30, which directly blocks the project's permit pathway regardless of other approvals. The project's 300 MW load drives an assumed backup power configuration of 121 Tier 2 diesel generators at 2,500 kW each, yielding an estimated NOx potential to emit of 1,067 tpy, which exceeds the 100 tpy major-source threshold and triggers a federal Title V operating permit requirement. The Title V major-source finding rests on unverified assumptions about generator fuel, tier, and runtime; the critic notes that alternative designs could reduce NOx below the threshold, but the current computed value stands as the basis for applicability. Local politics via the county moratorium create an immediate, absolute barrier to any data center application processing, while the federal air permitting requirement adds a major, assumption-dependent layer that would only become relevant if the moratorium were lifted.
